report:
Reviewed the full symbol_keyed_interfaces claim, five ordinary implementation associations and the one associated TODO test. Requirements: public checking queries accept definition identities; derive definition scope and environment internally; expose signatures as the main cross-item interface with separately keyed field/member detail when needed; and do not expose bodies or checking temporaries as cross-item semantic interfaces. Captured checking design and the linked architectural-foundations RFD, including its distinction between semantic boundaries and coarse-input reexecution followed by backdating.

Implementation assessment: LocalFnSym::sig takes only self and db, opens its own CST and initializes Check/Resolver from self.scope. For associated functions open_owner follows self.owner to trait/impl signature products, opening their binders and environment rather than accepting ambient caller parameters. Its return is a Stashed binder containing FnSig types, receiver and parameter environment. LocalImplSym::sig similarly derives its source, scope, generics, self type, trait reference and predicates from the impl symbol. Struct fields is a distinct tracked query keyed by LocalStructSym, reopening self.sig's parameters. Trait items is a distinct tracked LocalTraitSym query; impl items follows the same design. Both call associated::lower_items with their own source and owner generics. This crate-private lowering helper is not itself a public query contract accepting arbitrary ambient state: its public owning queries supply those arguments. It returns item symbols and an owner binder, not eagerly checked member bodies. The keyed associated-item helper queries likewise derive scope and source from owner identity plus member key.

Captured FnSymbol/TraitSymbol dispatch confirms the wrappers select local or external products using the typed definition identity. The captured external function signature entry takes SymExt and derives the metadata key from its crate/index; no caller scope or inference state is an argument. Captured Resolver::new establishes fresh ribs from the supplied definition scope, and Check::new creates query-local output storage and predicate accumulation. Check::finish returns the semantic product rather than the mutable checking context. LocalFnSym::body is a separate symbol-keyed demand, obtains the signature as input and creates its own InferCtx and scope. That body demand is available to clients requesting the body itself; it is not a signature interface supplied to a different definition. The inspected signature/detail methods do not call function body queries. These observations establish the represented source boundaries, not an exhaustive dynamic absence-of-body-reads proof.

The sole associated test todo::checking_symbol_keyed_interfaces has no behavioral assertions. Its explicit deferred matrix asks for signature and body requests as distinct symbol-keyed trace roots, rejection of ambient caller parameters/callee-body reads, and reuse after interface-preserving edits. Completing it requires source-backed caller/callee fixtures, trace observations at the real query boundaries, and persistent revisions comparing interface results and downstream execution. The linked RFD permits a coarse input to reexecute a producer if equal results backdate; the eventual edit assertions should preserve this distinction. The current TODO honestly retains these verification requirements rather than treating the absence of assertions as success. No N/A or ordinary test execution evidence exists for this anchor's current test set.

Commands executed: fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions; source and full associated-test inspection; review read captures for design/RFD, typed query dispatch, Check context, resolver construction and the external function signature entry. No tests or build were run by this reviewer, and central suite results are separate evidence. No source changes and no new suspected defect requiring reproduction. No requested edits; complete runtime and incremental verification remains explicitly deferred by the existing TODO.
